meta.case_name: DevCo (Redefining Medical Device Global Marketing Strategy)

prompt.context: DevCo is a global medical device manufacturer headquartered in the US with operations in more than 60 countries. The company produces a range of medical devices and data management tools. They have always been a market leader and commanded premium pricing; however, intensified competitive pressure from lower-cost manufacturers and increased customer price sensitivity have negatively impacted margins and market share. In response, the CMO repositioned part of the high-end product line for cost-conscious customers and led an acquisition to develop a lower-cost product line. While the expanded portfolio is robust, the product lines lack differentiation, creating customer confusion and impacting financial performance. Product development, marketing, and sales are managed at the product level. DevCo has engaged Deloitte to develop a new portfolio strategy and redefine the go-to-market strategy to position DevCo for continued market leadership and growth.
prompt.question: You are a Senior Consultant on the Deloitte team. You will be asked a series of questions: (1) What factors should DevCo consider when evaluating its product portfolio and go-to-market strategy? (2) DevCo has three primary product lines (A, B, and C) — which is most attractive? (3) How many units of a new product (NewPro) does DevCo need to sell to be profitable? Would you launch it? (4) What should DevCo consider when deciding to launch NewPro for Product Line B? If you were the CEO, would you launch NewPro?

clarifying_info.q: What types of customers does DevCo serve?
clarifying_info.a: DevCo serves a range of customers with varying preferences — some value high-end features and support, others are more price-sensitive.

clarifying_info.q: Are costs variable or fixed for the product lines?
clarifying_info.a: Assume all costs are variable when using the financial data.

clarifying_info.q: What is the price and cost structure for NewPro?
clarifying_info.a: NewPro has a suggested price of $200 with a $15 rebate per unit. Manufacturing cost is $115 per unit, marketing cost is $20 per unit, and fixed launch costs are $20,000,000.
NewPro will be positioned as 'leading edge' with a high-touch support model and sold through third-party distributors that Product Line B currently uses.

exhibits.title: DevCo Data Sheet — Financial Information and Product Line Details
exhibits.shows: Financial breakdown (Revenue, COGS, SG&A, Cost of Capital, 2013 estimated growth) for Product Lines A, B, and C for 2011 and 2012, plus a product line information table showing features/functionality, product support description, product life, sales channel, and price point for each line.

financial_table.note: All numbers in millions of dollars (USD)

product_line_table.support: Always on call; High touch approach
Readily available support; Limited on-site availability
Always on call; Limited on-site availability

framework: Customer Mix: Identify types of customers and what they need (product attributes, engagement approach, willingness to pay)
Competition: Understand what differentiates DevCo from lower-cost rivals and how to leverage it to protect/gain share
Brand: Determine how to position each product line on features, price, and channel to protect the DevCo brand
Channel: Evaluate which distribution channels to use and relevant regulatory considerations
Product: Assess customer willingness to pay for features; identify which products are 'good enough' for different segments
Financial Impact: Analyze revenue and profitability by product line
Strategic Priorities: Use product positioning and customer engagement to support continued market leadership and broad portfolio strategy
Organization Structure: Assess whether the current product-level org can support the future portfolio strategy
Global Footprint: Account for country-specific needs and regulations affecting product requirements and GTM
Evolving Environment: Address market trends such as Health Care Reform and growth of emerging markets

questions.prompt: Question 1: What factors should DevCo consider when evaluating its product portfolio and go-to-market strategy?
questions.guidance: A good answer covers external environment (customers, competition, brand, channel, product features, financial impact). A great answer also addresses strategic priorities, organizational structure, global footprint, and evolving market trends (Health Care Reform, emerging markets). The candidate should be structured and MECE, ideally proposing a clear framework before diving in.

questions.prompt: Question 2: Which product line (A, B, or C) is most attractive for DevCo?
questions.guidance: Candidate should build income statements for 2012 using the data sheet. A good answer calculates 2012 operating income and margin. A great answer extends the analysis to 2013 using growth rates (since all costs are variable, operating income grows at the same rate as revenue). Key findings: Product Line C has the highest operating margin % in all years (47% in 2011, 38% in 2012/2013) and the fastest revenue growth (50% in 2013). Product Line B has the largest absolute operating income but the lowest margin. Qualitative factors (support model, product life, channel) can also be used to support the argument.

math.setup: Build income statements for 2011, 2012, and 2013 (2013 = 2012 x (1 + growth rate), since all costs variable). Operating Income = Revenue - COGS - SG&A. Operating Margin % = Operating Income / Revenue.
steps: Product Line A 2012: Revenue $1,000M - COGS $600M - SG&A $150M = Op. Income $250M; Margin 25%
Product Line B 2012: Revenue $2,250M - COGS $1,700M - SG&A $225M = Op. Income $325M; Margin 14%
Product Line C 2012: Revenue $600M - COGS $250M - SG&A $120M = Op. Income $230M; Margin 38%
Product Line A 2013 (x1.20): Revenue $1,200M - COGS $720M - SG&A $180M = Op. Income $300M; Margin 25%
Product Line B 2013 (x1.05): Revenue $2,363M - COGS $1,785M - SG&A $236M = Op. Income $341M; Margin 14%
Product Line C 2013 (x1.50): Revenue $900M - COGS $375M - SG&A $180M = Op. Income $345M; Margin 38%
Cost of Capital is extraneous — do not use it in the analysis
math.answer: Product Line C is most attractive: highest operating margin % (38%) in 2012 and 2013, and fastest revenue growth (50% in 2013). Using multi-year perspective, Product Line C also approaches Product Line B in absolute operating income by 2013 ($345M vs. $341M).

questions.prompt: Question 3: How many units of NewPro does DevCo need to sell to be profitable? Would you launch it?
questions.guidance: Straightforward breakeven analysis. Candidate must identify net price (after rebate), variable cost per unit (manufacturing + marketing), and contribution margin, then divide fixed costs by contribution margin. Follow-up: assess whether 400,000 units is achievable — NewPro break-even revenue is ~$74M, only ~3.3% of Product Line B's 2012 revenue ($2,250M), suggesting the volume target is viable. Bonus: note that 100% rebate execution is conservative; lower execution raises margin and lowers break-even. Also note NewPro's contribution margin (27% on net price) is nearly double Product Line B's average margin (14%).

math.setup: Net Price = List Price - Rebate. Variable Cost = Manufacturing + Marketing. Contribution Margin = Net Price - Variable Cost. Break-Even Units = Fixed Costs / Contribution Margin.
steps: Viability check: 400,000 x $185 = $74M net revenue; $74M / $2,250M = 3.3% of Product Line B 2012 revenue
math.answer: 400,000 units. The volume required represents only ~3.3% of Product Line B's existing revenue base, suggesting it is achievable in Year 1.

questions.prompt: Question 4: What should DevCo consider when deciding to launch NewPro for Product Line B? As CEO of all three product lines, would you launch NewPro?
questions.guidance: A good answer draws on prior analysis: investment priorities (Product Line B has low margin and slow growth vs. Product Line C), product overlap risk (NewPro as 'leading edge' may cannibalize Product Line A and deepen customer confusion), and support model mismatch (Product Line B uses distributors with limited on-site support; NewPro's high-touch model requires additional investment). A great answer also examines mitigation strategies: launching NewPro under Product Line A instead (better fit with leading-edge positioning and high-touch sales force), assessing whether current Product Line B customers are demanding this product (making launch a competitive necessity), and noting that the decision depends on whether the direct sales force for Product Line A is an appropriate channel for NewPro. Overall, most factors suggest NOT launching NewPro under Product Line B in its current form.

brainstorming.prompt: What qualitative factors beyond the financial analysis should influence the portfolio and NewPro launch decision?

categories.name: Brand & Positioning
ideas: NewPro as 'leading edge' conflicts with Product Line B's mid-range/entry-level brand identity
Overlap between NewPro and Product Line A products could create customer confusion
Consistent brand story across product lines is critical for premium pricing retention

categories.name: Channel & Support Model
ideas: Product Line B uses distributors with limited on-site support; NewPro requires high-touch model
Adding a high-touch support requirement to a distributor channel demands incremental investment
Sales force alignment (direct vs. distributor) affects customer reach and service quality

categories.name: Organization & Operations
ideas: Product-level org structure creates silos; portfolio rationalization requires cross-product coordination
Capacity and resourcing for NewPro launch must be assessed against existing product lines
Leadership alignment across product lines is needed before launch

categories.name: Strategic Fit
ideas: Investment dollars are limited; Product Line C (highest margin, fastest growth) may deserve priority
NewPro may be better housed under Product Line A than Product Line B
If existing Product Line B customers demand NewPro, not launching risks competitive loss

categories.name: Market & Regulatory
ideas: Country-specific regulations may affect NewPro's go-to-market requirements in international markets
Health Care Reform trends may shift customer willingness to pay for premium features
Emerging markets may favor lower-cost products over leading-edge innovation

recommendation: Prioritize investment in Product Line C — it has the highest operating margin (38%) and fastest growth (50% projected for 2013), making it the most attractive line for DevCo
Do not launch NewPro under Product Line B in its current form — the 'leading edge' positioning, high-touch support requirement, and distributor channel are misaligned
risks: Launching NewPro under Product Line B risks deepening product overlap with Product Line A and increasing customer confusion
If existing Product Line B customers require NewPro-type features, not launching may accelerate churn to competitors
Shifting investment to Product Line C may be perceived as abandoning Product Line B customers and channel partners
next_steps: Evaluate launching NewPro under Product Line A, where leading-edge positioning and high-touch sales force are already established
Conduct customer research to determine whether Product Line B buyers are actively demanding NewPro features
Develop a clear portfolio rationalization roadmap to reduce overlap between lines A, B, and C and redefine go-to-market by customer segment
